To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
local infusion of methacholine into one leg of an anaesthetised insulin-infused rat increases glucose uptake into muscle in the test leg, but not in the contra-lateral leg.
local methacholine infusion into one leg of anaesthetised rats, during systemic insulin infusion, increased muscle glucose uptake in that leg only.
local methacholine infusion in vivo augments insulin-mediated glucose uptake into muscle by increasing the number of capillary beds recruited to insulin.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the regulation of glucose metabolism and the role of the vasculature in the control of insulin action.
understanding the role of nitric oxide in the control of blood flow and glucose uptake in muscle.
understanding the mechanisms by which insulin enhances glucose uptake into skeletal muscle.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the vasodilator effects of insulin and methacholine are different and that the latter enhances insulin-mediated glucose disposal by augmenting capillarization.

methacholine but neither bradykinin nor insulin, each alone, increased capillary blood flow and glucose uptake, but that local methacholine with insulin enhanced glucose uptake by increasing capillary recruitment.
methacholine but no bradykinin augments capillary recruitment to enhance insulin action in vivo.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
methacholine enhances insulin action in skeletal muscle, but bradykinin does not.
the nitric oxide-dependent vasodilator methacholine enhances insulin action in muscle in vivo, whereas other nitric oxide-dependent and nitric oxide-independent vasodilators do not.
insulin-mediated glucose disposal is limited by capillary recruitment and that this limitation is overcome by methacholine.
The main takeaway from our work is that
methacholin, a non-selective muscarinic receptor agonist, can increase capillary recruitment in muscle in vivo and that this effect can enhance insulin action.
the vasodilatory response is not the same as the capillary recruitment response and that the two can be dissociated.

the nitric oxide donor sodium nitroprusside (SNP) and the nitric oxide synthase (NOS) inhibitor L-NG-Nitroarginine Methyl Ester (L-NAME) have opposite effects on the vasculature in muscle, and these effects can be reversed by methacholine.
